🤏 smolmaxxing

 

 

 🎉 Over 5,000 downloads on Hugging Face 🎉 
 📰 Featured in Tproger , GIGAZINE and TechnoEdge 

 Run the biggest language model you can on the smallest hardware you own. 

TV boxes, old phones and tablets, single-board computers and routers all have a CPU, some RAM and flash storage that sit idle most of the day. smolmaxxing finds the biggest model each of them can really run, then pushes it further with custom kernels, careful memory use and weights streamed from flash. Every number in this repo was measured on the device itself.

 Eight devices so far

 
 
 
 📺 Xiaomi TV Box S (3rd Gen) 
 Amlogic S7D, 4× Cortex-A55 1.9 GB RAM (about 1 GB usable) · Android 14, no root 
Everyday: Qwen3.5-2B at 7.7 tok/s 
Biggest: Ling-mini-2.0, 16B, at 5.1 tok/s 
 Full results →

 Apple A7, 2 cores 1 GB RAM (about 700 MB usable) · iOS 12.5.7, jailbroken 
Everyday: Bonsai-1.7B (1-bit) at 24-26 tok/s 
Biggest: Ling-mini-2.0, 16B, at 2.6-4.5 tok/s 
 Full results →

 MediaTek Dimensity 900, 2× Cortex-A78 + 6× A55 7.4 GB RAM (about 3 GB free) · Android 13, no root 
Everyday: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 4.9-5.7 tok/s 
Biggest: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B at 2.6-3.1 tok/s 
 Full results →

 Snapdragon 710, 2× Kryo 360 (A76-class) + 6× A55, no dotprod 6 GB RAM (about 3.3 GB free) · Android 10, no root 
Everyday: Qwen3-0.6B (Q8 0) at 14.6 tok/s 
Biggest: Qwen3-1.7B (Q8 0) at 5.7 tok/s

 📲 Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (2024) 
 Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 1× Cortex-X4 + 5× A720 + 2× A520 12 GB RAM, 3.0 GB RSS for server + model · Android 17 
Everyday: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 12-16 tok/s 
Biggest: the same 35B MoE, from the phone GGUF (12.3 GB) 
 Submission → · setup scripts 
 Submitted by drqebas-crypto 
 
 
 📲 Infinix GT 20 Pro (2024) 
 MediaTek Dimensity 8200 Ultimate, 1× Cortex-A78 + 3× A78 + 4× A55 8 GB RAM · XOS 16.3.0 
Everyday: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 3.1 tok/s 
Biggest: the same 35B MoE, from the phone GGUF (no log yet) 
 Submission → 
 Submitted by kouunbliss319 
 
 
 

The TV box and the iPad run 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on about 1 GB of RAM, and the phone runs 35B and 80B ones with about 3 GB free. They all keep only part of each model in memory and read the rest from flash as it's needed. The BuzzTV box, measured by a contributor, is the first 32-bit device: the same cores as the Xiaomi box, but a 32-bit Android that rules out the arm64-only kernels. The Kindle runs a chatbot and a coding assistant on one 32-bit Cortex-A9 with 512 MB of RAM. The Realme 5 Pro, also measured by a contributor, is the first device without the dot-product extension: its A76-class cores carry fp16 but not dotprod, so it runs the plain-NEON build and its numbers show what that costs. Two more contributors ran the phone's 35B mixture-of-experts on their own phones: a Galaxy S24 Ultra on a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 at 12-16 tok/s, the fastest 35B run here (drqebas-crypto), and an Infinix GT 20 Pro at 3.1 tok/s (kouunbliss319).

The chart below compares the two 1 GB devices size class by size class; the phone plays in a bigger league, and its results are in docs/phone.md.

 

More devices (single-board computers, routers, more phones) are coming. The techniques aren't tied to one box: the 1-bit kernel needs only basic NEON, and the flash streaming works on any Linux or Android device with more model than RAM.

 Got a small device? Run a model on it and submit your numbers: we'll add them to the results.

 

 How it works

All of it is a patch on llama.cpp. The main ideas:

- Kernels built for the chip. A 1-bit lookup-table kernel, repacked 2-bit and ternary formats for the Cortex-A55, and versions of them for the A7, which has no dot-product instructions.
- Less RAM per model. Most of a small model's vocabulary is rarely used, so we drop those output rows. On the TV, a "headless" mode also stops the launcher and Google services while a model runs.
- Experts paged from flash. A mixture-of-experts model only uses a few experts per token. We keep the popular ones in RAM, read the others from flash on demand and prefetch the next layer's. This is how 8B and 16B models run on 1 GB, and 35B and 80B models on a phone.
- Streaming for dense models bigger than RAM, at the flash's full speed.

docs/how-it-works.md has every technique with its measured gain.

 Try it

The quickest start is a ready-made model file from Hugging Face. The TV box and iPad files need the patched llama.cpp (stock llama.cpp can't load their pruned heads); the phone files load anywhere, but their speeds need the patch's expert pager.

- TV box or another ARMv8.2 Android device: docs/tv-box-setup.md
- Chat on the TV itself, offline: the SmolChat app starts the model server at every boot and opens the chat from the TV home screen, with no computer or internet: docs/tv-box-setup.md
- 32-bit ARM (armv7) Android device: docs/buzztv-xr4500.md
- Jailbroken iPad on iOS 12: ipad-air/README.md
- Android phone with 8 GB of RAM: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (12.3 GB) and Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (27.6 GB, two files), set up as in docs/phone.md.
- ARM device without the dot-product extension ( asimddp missing from /proc/cpuinfo ): docs/realme-5pro.md
- All model files and how to rebuild them: docs/models.md
